title: Filtered colimits preserve weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets
statement:
Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $X,Y:I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be diagrams of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and $f:X\to Y$ a natural transformation. Assume that each $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, meaning a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups after geometric realization [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Then the induced map on degreewise colimits
$$\varinjlim_{i\in I}X_i\longrightarrow\varinjlim_{i\in I}Y_i$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. No injectivity hypothesis is imposed on the transition maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to the small filtered category $I$. It supplies a nonempty directed set $A$, a functor $F:A\to I$, and the clause that every colimit cocone on a diagram over $I$ remains a colimit after whiskering with $F$. Whisker $X$, $Y$, and $f$ with $F$; each component of the resulting natural transformation is still a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0032 (lemma-directed-category-system), clause (1); directed sets are preorders, not necessarily partial orders (definition-directed-set).

proof.text: The directed set $A$ need not be antisymmetric. Put $a\sim a^{\prime}$ if $a\le a^{\prime}$ and $a^{\prime}\le a$, and let $B=A/{\sim}$ with $[a]\le[a^{\prime}]$ if $a\le a^{\prime}$. This is a small nonempty partial order; a common upper bound in $A$ gives one in $B$, hence every finite subset of $B$ has an upper bound. Choose representatives $r:B\to A$. They form a monotone functor since the quotient order is independent of representatives. For any diagram $Z:A\to\mathrm{sSet}$, cocones on $Zr$ and on $Z$ correspond: a cocone $(\mu_b)$ on $Zr$ extends to the legs $\lambda_a=\mu_{[a]}\circ Z(a\to r([a]))$. If $a\le a^{\prime}$, the two composites from $a$ to $r([a^{\prime}])$ are the same arrow in the preorder, giving the cocone equation. Restriction and extension are inverse: $r([a])\sim a$ gives inverse arrows, while $[r(b)]=b$ and the arrow $r(b)\to r(b)$ is the identity. These operations preserve the apex and commute with postcomposition; by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a colimit cocone on $Z$ restricts to a colimit cocone on $Zr$.

source.place: Definition directed-set and elementary antisymmetrization and cocone calculation, written here.

proof.text: Apply the directed-colimit clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to $XFr,YFr:B\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and $fr$. Step 2 proves that $B$ is small, nonempty and partially ordered with finite upper bounds. Each component of $fr$ is $f_{F(r(b))}$, so is a weak homotopy equivalence by hypothesis. The resulting degreewise colimit map $h:C_X=\operatorname{colim}_B XFr\to C_Y=\operatorname{colim}_B YFr$ is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. No condition on transition maps has been used.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.8.3 (00XE), filtered-colimit assertion specialized to a directed partial order; the cited existing node states precisely this specialization.

proof.text: Let $(L_X,\iota_i)$ and $(L_Y,\kappa_i)$ be the original degreewise colimit cocones and $g:L_X\to L_Y$ the map induced by $f$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] and the cocone correspondence of step 2 show that $(L_X,\iota_{F(r(b))})$ and $(L_Y,\kappa_{F(r(b))})$ are colimit cocones over $B$. If $j_b,k_b$ denote the legs into $C_X,C_Y$, the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives isomorphisms $u_X:C_X\to L_X$, $u_Y:C_Y\to L_Y$ characterized by $u_Xj_b=\iota_{F(r(b))}$ and $u_Yk_b=\kappa_{F(r(b))}$. Both $g u_X$ and $u_Yh$, after composition with $j_b$, equal $\kappa_{F(r(b))}f_{F(r(b))}$, so uniqueness gives $g u_X=u_Yh$. Thus $g=u_Yh u_X^{-1}$. A simplicial isomorphism realizes to a homeomorphism (realization applies its inverse), hence induces bijections on components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group. The defining maps on these invariants for $g$ are composites of those for $u_Y,h,u_X^{-1}$, so $g$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.
